harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Redis/Sentinel is fully operational across node1-node3. node1 began as primary; the controlled outage promoted node2, and node1 returned as a synchronized replica. Redis and Sentinel use authenticated TLS-only endpoints, all data and services survived sequential node reboots, and the final cluster is healthy with node2 primary and two online replicas.
actions_performed: Installed Redis 7 and Sentinel on all nodes.
Configured Redis TLS on port 6379 and Sentinel TLS on port 26379.
Created root-only administrative credentials at /root/redis-admin.env on node1.
Validated automatic failover and continued writes during node1’s outage.
Restored node1 and verified its automatic reintegration as a synchronized replica.
Safely restarted node1, node3, and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and recovery.

evidence.requirement: Initial node1 primary with node2 and node3 replicas; infra:proof=ready
evidence.summary: node1 reported master with two online replicas; both replicas reported master_link=up and contained infra:proof=ready.

evidence.requirement: Authenticated TLS-only Redis and Sentinel services with administrative credentials
evidence.summary: All nodes expose only cache-network listeners on 6379/26379, authenticate successfully over verified TLS 1.3, reject unauthenticated requests, and node1’s credential file is root:root mode 600.
Sentinel reports two peer Sentinels and two replicas, establishing the three-Sentinel deployment with quorum.

evidence.requirement: Automatic promotion while the original primary is unavailable
evidence.summary: node1 Redis was stopped, Sentinel elected and promoted node2, node3 remained online, existing data was readable, and infra:failover=verified was written during the outage.

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary returns as a synchronized replica
evidence.summary: Restored node1 became a replica of node2 with master_link=up and contained both the original and failover-era data.
Healthy baseline and boot ID 72e73f96... were captured, reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to ed1ed91d..., and services, data, synchronization, two replicas, and Sentinel quorum recovered.
Healthy baseline and boot ID 8d1d94e2... were captured, reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to 1f96a81d..., and services, data, synchronization, two replicas, and Sentinel quorum recovered.
Healthy primary baseline and boot ID 63f96994... were captured, reboot was acknowledged, boot ID changed to f155f6e1..., and node2 recovered as primary with both replicas online and all data intact.
Redis and Sentinel are active and enabled everywhere; node2 is primary, node1/node3 are synchronized replicas, all Sentinels agree on node2, and both proof keys are present on every node.
